skill.name: frontend-aesthetics
skill.description: Guides AI agents to create distinctive frontend visual design with stronger typography, color, motion, backgrounds, and context-specific style.
skill.summary: Helps AI agents design frontend interfaces that feel specific, polished, and less generic.
skill.author: Crossbill-Highlights

security_audit.summary: The five static system-reconnaissance alerts are false positives. The cited lines contain frontend design guidance about typography, color, backgrounds, and avoiding generic AI aesthetics, with no system probing or malicious instructions.

static_findings.snippet: You tend to converge toward generic, "on distribution" outputs. In frontend design,this creates what
- Typography: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Ari
- Backgrounds: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors. Layer CSS gradien
Interpret creatively and make unexpected choices that feel genuinely designed for the context. Vary

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 5 discusses avoiding generic AI-looking frontend output. It does not request host inspection, environment probing, credential access, or any system reconnaissance behavior.
Line 8 gives typography advice for visual design. It contains no instruction to enumerate system data, execute commands, or inspect local configuration.
Line 11 recommends visual background treatments such as gradients and patterns. This is frontend styling guidance, not reconnaissance or operational abuse.
Line 13 is a section heading about avoiding generic AI-generated aesthetics. It does not contain security-sensitive behavior or prompt-injection language.
Line 19 encourages creative, context-specific frontend choices. The word critical is used as emphasis for design quality, not as an override or system instruction.

content.value_statement: Many AI-built interfaces look generic and predictable. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward richer visual design choices.
actual_capabilities: Guides typography choices toward distinctive fonts and stronger visual character.
Encourages cohesive color themes with clear dominant colors and sharp accents.
Promotes purposeful motion for page loads, transitions, and micro-interactions.
Suggests layered backgrounds using gradients, patterns, and contextual effects.
Pushes designs away from common AI-generated layouts and color schemes.
Encourages context-specific visual decisions for each frontend project.
limitations: It provides design direction, not a complete design system by itself.
It does not include reusable components, assets, or implementation code.
It does not validate accessibility, performance, or responsive behavior automatically.
It depends on the agent and project context to apply the guidance well.

use_cases.title: Refresh a SaaS Interface
use_cases.description: Improve a dashboard or product screen that feels plain, repetitive, or too close to common AI output.

use_cases.title: Shape a Product Visual Direction
use_cases.description: Create a stronger aesthetic direction before building a new web app, prototype, or feature.

use_cases.title: Polish a Launch Page
use_cases.description: Make a first version feel more intentional through better type, color, motion, and background choices.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Basic Screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a more polished interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-aesthetics skill to improve this screen. Focus on typography, color, spacing, and one memorable visual detail.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Visual Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-aesthetics skill to propose a visual direction for this product. Include type style, palette, motion, and background treatment.

prompt_templates.title: Review for Generic AI Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Audit an existing interface for predictable design choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-aesthetics skill to review this interface. Identify generic patterns and replace them with context-specific visual choices.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Complete Experience
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a full page or workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-aesthetics skill to design this workflow end to end. Make the layout, typography, color, motion, and background feel cohesive.

output_examples.input: A plain analytics dashboard needs stronger visual identity.
output_examples.output: The result should use a tighter information hierarchy, a distinctive display typeface, restrained accent colors, and subtle state transitions.

output_examples.input: A startup landing page feels like a generic AI template.
output_examples.output: The result should introduce a stronger visual theme, custom section rhythm, contextual background texture, and more intentional hero composition.

output_examples.input: A product settings page needs polish without becoming decorative.
output_examples.output: The result should keep controls efficient while improving typography, spacing, contrast, and small motion cues for user actions.

best_practices: Provide product context, audience, and brand tone before asking for design changes.
Ask for concrete visual decisions, not only general polish or beauty.
Review accessibility and responsive behavior after applying aesthetic changes.
anti_patterns: Do not request a generic modern redesign without domain context.
Do not rely on purple gradients, default fonts, or repeated card layouts.
Do not add motion that slows core workflows or distracts from user tasks.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI agents make frontend interfaces feel more distinctive, intentional, and visually polished.

faq.question: Does it generate production code?
faq.answer: The skill gives design guidance. The agent may still write code when the surrounding task asks for implementation.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only for landing pages?
faq.answer: No. It can guide dashboards, app screens, settings pages, prototypes, and marketing pages.

faq.question: Does it replace accessibility review?
faq.answer: No. Accessibility, contrast, keyboard behavior, and responsive layout still need separate verification.

faq.question: Why avoid common fonts and gradients?
faq.answer: The skill tries to reduce predictable AI design patterns and create choices that better fit each project.
